name: @melra/cli

tools.name: melra_capabilities
tools.description: Report what this MELRA server can run and the policy in force. Call it once before melra_plan or melra_workflow_plan; it takes no input and changes nothing. Returns product, version and protocolVersion; tools; operations (the actions each operation kind supports); customEvidence (verifier names allowed in custom evidence); workflowNodes (node types for workflow definitions); and policy, including mode, workspaceRoot, unhinged, mutations, allowedCommands, deniedTraits, allowedDomains, circuitBreaker and credential names.

tools.name: melra_plan
tools.description: Plan one bounded operation without running it: MELRA evaluates policy and stores the task in its own records only, so nothing outside MELRA changes until it runs. Send a goal, one operation and requiredEvidence, and leave constraints empty. Returns the task with its effect contract and status planned, awaiting_approval (approval holds the challenge) or policy_blocked (a normal result; policyDecision.reason says why); an invalid request, such as one naming an unregistered verifier or a file evidence path outside the workspace, fails the call instead. Keep its id: it is the taskId for melra_execute, melra_task_status, melra_task_cancel and melra_receipt. For dependent steps use melra_workflow_plan.

goal.description: Why this task is being run, in one human-readable sentence.

operation.description: The one effect to run: a kind (file, terminal, browser, memory, computer, http or system), an action (melra_capabilities lists each kind's actions) and that kind's fields. MELRA classifies it as read, mutate or destructive; policy then allows it, asks for approval or denies it.

constraints.description: Leave empty. Freeform prose cannot be enforced, so a non-empty array is denied with freeform_constraints_not_enforceable. Express real limits as forbiddenEffects, budget, or requiredEvidence.

forbiddenEffects.description: Effects this task must never take. Denied before the adapter runs, and honoured even in unhinged mode.

budget.description: maxDurationMs (100-900000, default 120000) is timed from the first attempt: once it passes, no retry starts and a terminal run or browser, computer or http operation is aborted. maxRetries (0-10, default 2) retries only reads whose adapter throws. maxSteps (1-100, default 10) limits nothing.

requiredEvidence.description: Predicates that must hold after execution for the task to be verified_success. A non-read operation needs them unless MELRA derives a default for it; outside unsafe-local mode one with neither is denied with mutation_requires_evidence. An adapter that succeeded while a predicate failed is partial, never success. A semantic predicate is never answered by MELRA: the task waits in waiting_user and fails closed at expiry. Beside semantic, a destructive effect also needs file_exists, file_absent, file_hash or http_resource_matches, or outside unsafe-local mode it is denied with semantic_only_destructive; semantic beside reconciliation is denied with semantic_evidence_not_reconcilable.

question.description: A yes/no question about this effect's result, for a judge outside MELRA. Stored and shown as written, minus secret shapes.

artifacts.description: Dotted paths into this operation's recorded result (json.total, path), never content.

reconciliation.description: How to settle this effect if MELRA never learns whether it happened — a request that went out and was never answered, or a crash mid-flight. Read against the facts that were true before the call (idempotencyKey, url, method), never against a response, because there is none. Declaring these makes the executionGuarantee reconciliation-required instead of at-most-once.

question.description: A yes/no question about this effect's result, for a judge outside MELRA. Stored and shown as written, minus secret shapes.

artifacts.description: Dotted paths into this operation's recorded result (json.total, path), never content.

identity.description: Who is asking, and on whose behalf. Recorded on the task and every receipt, and matched against policy.capabilities when the operator has issued grants. Omitted means the implicit local principal.

tools.name: melra_execute
tools.description: Run one task melra_plan returned, by taskId: MELRA re-evaluates policy, so a plan made under a looser policy is still refused, then runs the operation, checks its requiredEvidence and records a receipt. If the plan returned an approval challenge with a phrase, pass approval with its approvalId and exact phrase; the phrase is scoped to that one task and expires. Only reads are retried, and a recovery_required task is reconciled, never re-run: it stays recovery_required while its provider cannot be reached (task.error reconciliation_inconclusive, ask again later) or while MELRA refuses to ask its reconciliation (reconciliation_unanswerable:<reason>, which asking again will not change). Returns { task, output?, receipt?, certificate? } with the outcome in task.status. For workflow steps use melra_workflow_advance instead.

taskId.description: The id melra_plan returned. Only a planned or awaiting_approval task can run; a policy_blocked one comes back unchanged, a recovery_required one is reconciled rather than re-run, and any other status fails with task_not_executable:<status>. Unknown ids fail with task_not_found.

approval.description: The awaiting_approval task's challenge as {approvalId, phrase}, phrase copied exactly. Omit it for a planned task, or once an operator has approved with `melra approve`. In enforced mode never send it: for a task that needs approval it is refused (approval_in_band_refused).

tools.name: melra_task_status
tools.description: Read one task's stored record by taskId (from melra_plan, or a workflow node's taskIds), in any status, policy_blocked and cancelled included, without changing or waiting on it. Returns the task: status, policyDecision, any approval challenge and approvedBy, the redacted request and result, error, attempts, receiptIds, certificateId and timestamps. Use it to re-check a task after melra_task_cancel or from another session, or to re-read a pending challenge. Use melra_receipt for receipts and the certificate, and melra_workflow_status for a whole workflow run.

taskId.description: The id melra_plan returned, or one of a workflow node's taskIds from melra_workflow_status. An unknown id fails with task_not_found.

tools.name: melra_task_cancel
tools.description: Cancel one task by taskId and return its record; nothing that already happened is undone. A planned or awaiting_approval task becomes cancelled and can no longer be executed. A task running in this MELRA process is sent an abort, which interrupts terminal run, browser, computer and http operations; the returned record predates it, so read the outcome with melra_task_status. Any other task, including one running in another process, is returned unchanged without error, and so is one another process starts at the same moment, which then runs: check the returned status. On a workflow step's task that has not started it acts as a denial: the next melra_workflow_advance fails the run and offers the compensations of the steps already done, each for its own approval, unless another step's outcome is unknown, which leaves the run recovery_required; on a compensation's task it stops the unwind, and the run becomes recovery_required. melra_workflow_cancel ends a run without compensating.

taskId.description: The id melra_plan returned for the task to cancel. Cancelling a workflow step's task before it runs fails its run at the next advance, which then offers its compensations, unless another step's outcome is unknown (then recovery_required); cancelling a compensation's task stops the unwind (recovery_required). melra_workflow_cancel ends a run without compensating. An unknown id fails with task_not_found.

tools.name: melra_receipt
tools.description: Read a task's audit trail: returns { receipts, certificate? }. Pass taskId for all of that task's receipts plus its certificate, or receiptId for one receipt plus its task's certificate; receiptId wins if both are given. Each receipt records the capability, target, effect, principal, policy decision with any approval, timings, success, redacted observed effect and evidence; the certificate gives the overall result, such as VERIFIED_SUCCESS, PARTIAL or RECOVERY_REQUIRED. Use it to show what a task did; use melra_task_status for its current state.

taskId.description: The id melra_plan returned, or a workflow node's taskId: gets all of that task's receipts plus its certificate. An unknown id, or a task with no receipts yet, returns an empty list. Give this or receiptId.

receiptId.description: One receipt's id, from the task's receiptIds or melra_execute's receipt: gets that receipt plus its task's certificate. Takes precedence over taskId; an unknown id fails with receipt_not_found.

tools.name: melra_workflow_plan
tools.description: Validate a multi-step workflow definition and create a new run without executing anything: MELRA writes only its own records and plans no tasks; nothing outside MELRA changes until the run is advanced. Planning fails on the graph errors it checks (workflow_* codes, such as a dependency cycle), a step melra_plan would fail on, a condition, until or delegation check no registered verifier can ask (evidence_verifier_unavailable:<name>) or on a file path outside the workspace (evidence_path_outside_workspace), or a step policy denies (workflow_policy_blocked:<nodeId>); steps needing approval ask during advance. Returns the run, planned with every node pending; its id is the workflowId, and no tool lists runs. For one operation use melra_plan.

definition.description: The workflow: schemaVersion "1.0.0", an id (UUID) and positive version you choose, a name, and 1-500 nodes linked by dependsOn, of the types melra_capabilities lists under workflowNodes. Different content under an existing id and version fails with workflow_definition_conflict; bump version.

tools.name: melra_workflow_advance
tools.description: Run a workflow run's next wave; use it, not melra_execute, for workflow steps, calling again for later waves. It starts all ready nodes concurrently, each step under melra_execute's policy, approval and verification. Once the run has failed (a forward node failed, or was denied while no other's outcome is unknown), only compensations run, in reverse definition order, stopping at one that fails or is denied; otherwise nodes still waiting are offered again beside the newly ready ones, unless a waiting step's task was denied or otherwise moved since the last advance: then only the waiting nodes are offered, so nothing new starts on a run that may now fail. Approval waits return challenges in tasks; human_input and delegation nodes wait with a prompt. A step an earlier advance planned or ran without recording it (its commit failed) is taken up by its idempotency key, as recovery reads it: its challenge is offered again rather than a second one, its effect is never repeated, and one that failed or was denied stays so. Answer later via inputs and, outside enforced mode, approvals. Returns { run, tasks, events }, unchanged when nothing is due; a halted run fails with workflow_halted:<status>. A run left recovery_required names why in run.error: workflow_compensation_incomplete:<nodeId> for an unwind that stopped, workflow_condition_branch_conflict:<nodeId> for a condition whose branch not taken holds a step an interrupted advance ran that may have had an effect (settle one whose outcome is unknown with melra_execute, which reconciles it; one that took effect stays, so undo it by hand and end the run with melra_workflow_cancel, which compensates nothing), otherwise workflow_contains_unreconciled_mutation. A condition, a bounded_loop's until or a delegation's evidence its provider does not answer (a 503, a 401, no connection) decides nothing: the call fails with workflow_check_inconclusive:<nodeId>, the node waits with that check as its error (a delegation keeps its report), and each later call asks again. melra_workflow_cancel ends a run whose provider never answers, without compensating. A condition or delegation check MELRA refuses to ask (a URL token its source result cannot fill, a verifier no longer registered, a reserved path) fails its node instead (workflow_check_unresolvable:<nodeId>), and the run unwinds; a bounded_loop's until reads it as no and runs its next iteration. Either way the call fails, but a condition under which an interrupted advance ran a step whose outcome is unknown halts on that step instead of waiting or failing (recovery_required, as after a restart), so nothing unwinds past it.

workflowId.description: The run id melra_workflow_plan returned, not the definition's id. An unknown id fails with workflow_not_found; workflow_lease_held means something else holds the run's lease, so retry later; workflow_lease_lost means the run was taken over mid-advance once this advance's lease had lapsed, by another process's recovery or by an operator's halt or cancel, so advance again later.

approvals.description: Answers to challenges this run waits on, each {approvalId, phrase} copied from a waiting task's approval and matched by approvalId; unmatched entries are ignored. Must be empty in enforced mode (approval_in_band_refused).

inputs.description: Answers for awaiting_input nodes as {nodeId, value}, matched by nodeId and ignored for nodes this call does not run. A human_input value must fit the node's maxLength and any choices; a delegation value is the delegate's report, and any requiredEvidence on the node still decides.

tools.name: melra_workflow_status
tools.description: Read a workflow run in any status by workflowId without advancing or changing it; workflowId is the run id melra_workflow_plan returned, the same one melra_workflow_advance, melra_workflow_control and melra_workflow_cancel take. Returns the run: status (such as planned, running, awaiting_approval, awaiting_input, paused, suspended, verified_complete, failed, recovery_required or cancelled), error, stateVersion, definitionId, definitionVersion, timestamps, and nodes keyed by node id, each with its status, taskIds and, where set, approval, prompt, input, iterations and error. Check it before melra_workflow_advance to see what the run waits on; pass a node's taskIds to melra_task_status or melra_receipt for detail.

workflowId.description: The run id melra_workflow_plan returned, not the definition's id. An unknown id fails with workflow_not_found.

tools.name: melra_workflow_cancel
tools.description: End a workflow run by workflowId, the run id melra_workflow_plan returned. Its pending, ready and awaiting_approval nodes, compensations included, become cancelled and the run becomes cancelled; only once that is recorded are the tasks on those nodes, and any left planned or waiting under the run's steps, cancelled as melra_task_cancel would, so a cancel that fails changes no task, and one that fails after the run is cancelled reports it: cancel again to finish. Neither resume nor melra_workflow_advance continues it. It starts and undoes no effect: no compensation runs, and other nodes keep their status, though a step's task that another process starts at the same moment may still run (check it with melra_task_status). While an advance holds the run's lease, in this process or another, it fails with workflow_lease_held and changes nothing, so the steps that advance runs are recorded: retry once the advance returns. Do not stop a running step with melra_task_cancel to get the cancel in: that fails the step, and the advance still running it starts the run's unwind (its compensations run, or wait for approval) before this cancel can land. An advance that stalled past its lease, or died holding it, is taken over. The run's steps are first read again from their tasks, so what an advance that stalled, died or lost its commit ran is recorded on the cancelled run, and a step's task still running is cancelled as melra_task_cancel would: that step is recorded as still in flight (recovery_required, task_still_in_flight), not as cancelled, and one running in this process is recorded as it ends once it stops (tried again while something else holds the run's lease); cancelling the run again records any such step whose task has since ended, in any process. Works on paused, suspended and failed runs too. Returns the updated run: unchanged if already verified_complete, and if already cancelled changed only by recording such steps. To halt a run and continue later, use melra_workflow_control.

workflowId.description: The run id melra_workflow_plan returned, not the definition's id. An unknown id fails with workflow_not_found.

tools.name: melra_workflow_control
tools.description: Halt a workflow run or lift the halt, without changing node state. action pause or suspend (same behaviour; only the status name differs) sets the run's status to paused or suspended unless it is verified_complete, cancelled or failed; melra_workflow_advance then fails with workflow_halted:<status> while the run is halted. Halt between advances: while an advance holds the run's lease, in this process or another, pause, suspend and resume fail with workflow_lease_held and change nothing, so retry once it returns. resume needs a paused or suspended run, sets the status its nodes imply and runs nothing, so call melra_workflow_advance next. Returns the updated run. To end a run instead, use melra_workflow_cancel.

workflowId.description: The run id melra_workflow_plan returned, not the definition's id. An unknown id fails with workflow_not_found; workflow_lease_held means an advance holds the run's lease, so retry once it returns.

action.description: pause or suspend halts the run (same effect; only the status name differs) and fails with workflow_not_haltable on a verified_complete, cancelled or failed run. resume lifts either halt and runs nothing; on a run not halted it fails with workflow_not_paused.

instructions:
MELRA runs effects for you under policy: files, terminal, browser, HTTP, desktop, and memory. Use its tools instead of acting directly, and treat its results as the record of what happened.
For each action:
1. melra_capabilities (once): the operations available and the policy in force: allowed commands and domains, and whether mutations need approval.
2. melra_plan with a goal, one operation, and requiredEvidence. Nothing runs yet. status policy_blocked means refused: read the reason and change the request; the same request will be refused again. status awaiting_approval returns an approval challenge.
3. melra_execute with the taskId, plus the challenge id and its exact phrase if one was issued. Policy is checked again here.
4. Read the status. verified_success means the operation ran and every requiredEvidence check passed. partial means it ran but evidence did not hold. waiting_user means it ran and every check MELRA can make passed, but a semantic question (listed in judgements) waits for an answer from outside MELRA; nothing can answer one in this version, so at expiresAt it ends recovery_required for a change or partial for a read. recovery_required means a change may or may not have happened, or happened and its semantic question went unanswered (error semantic_judgement_expired): inspect the world before trying again, never re-run blindly. Only reads are retried for you.
5. melra_receipt returns the receipt and certificate when you need to show what was done.
Rules: any operation that is not a read must declare requiredEvidence describing how to confirm it (result_equals, result_contains, exit_code, file_exists, file_absent, file_hash, page_contains, url_matches, http_resource_matches, custom, semantic). custom takes a verifier name from customEvidence in melra_capabilities. Outside unsafe-local mode, semantic is never enough alone for a destructive effect, which also needs file_exists, file_absent, file_hash or http_resource_matches. Leave constraints empty; free-text constraints are refused because they cannot be enforced.
For multi-step jobs that must survive restarts, use melra_workflow_plan and melra_workflow_advance; each step still goes through the same policy, approval, and verification.
No tool lists all tasks or workflow runs, so keep the ids melra_plan and melra_workflow_plan return. melra_workflow_control pauses, suspends or resumes a run; melra_workflow_cancel ends it.
